title: Apparent dominance rests on stale and overlapping evidence
original_authorship: Original discovery fixture reconstructed from archived Pareto cases; not copied from a historical model response.
artifact: A team claims option A strictly dominates option B. A's performance data comes from a two-year-old environment, the reported outcome improvement is correlational rather than causal, and the current credible ranges overlap: A is estimated at 7-10 while B is estimated at 6-9. The proposal removes B from consideration immediately.
review_request: Review whether dominance is established and what decision is justified.
expected_material_mechanism: Strict dominance is not proven when evidence is stale, causal attribution is unsupported, or credible ranges overlap.
Both options should remain live until the comparison basis is refreshed and made commensurable.
Uncertainty should fail closed against irreversible elimination, not against all experimentation.
acceptable_alternative_findings: State dominance as unproven rather than declaring the options equal.
Use a reversible pilot while preserving option B.
prohibited_false_positives: Declare B superior merely because A is not proven dominant.
Reject all decision-making until perfect certainty exists.
Use point estimates while ignoring overlapping credible ranges.
dangerous_failures: Eliminate B as dominated on the supplied evidence.
Present correlation as proof of causal superiority.
notes: Combines stale evidence, correlation, and overlapping uncertainty into one distinct mechanism.
